law.form: Hapke (core/hapke.ts): single-lobed Henyey-Greenstein (c = 1) with a shadow-hiding opposition surge

normalisation.why: OMEGA albedo = I/F / cos(i), near nadir (e < 15 deg), i < 75 deg (Ody et al. 2012, §2.2, §3.1); the incidence within that range is a choice, its effect measured in `normalisationTried`

fittedTo.source: Mallama & Hilton (2018), "Computing apparent planetary magnitudes for The Astronomical Almanac", Astronomy and Computing 25, doi:10.1016/j.ascom.2018.08.002, arXiv:1808.01973, Eq. 6
fittedTo.leftOut: L(lambda_e), "RMS variation over longitude ... about 0.035 magnitude with excursions as large as 0.060", and L(Ls): their tables are in Mallama (2007), not read

calibrationSource: Mallama, Krobusek & Pavlov (2017), "Comprehensive wide-band magnitudes and albedos for the planets", Icarus 282, 19-33, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.09.023, arXiv:1609.05048, Table 7

luminance.why: CIE Y of the drawn colour (Rec. 709 luminance of linear sRGB) is brought to the V geometric albedo: the colour model joins the bands with straight lines, and Mars's spectrum curves up past 550 nm

method.grid: albedo.webp in 64 x 64 pixel block means (128 x 64)
method.viewer: on the equator; the Sun in the equatorial plane
method.band: the map is reflectance at 530 nm; Eq. 6 is Johnson V (about 550 nm)
